claims.text: The shot and its date: 'BLUEGILL Triple Prime (25 October 1962, 2359). The fourth attempt to launch the BLUEGILL device using a Thor missile was successful.'

Its place in the test series, from the report's own summary table: '25 Oct / BLUE GILL / FISHBOWL shot, submegaton, tens of kilometers over Johnston Island', sourced there to Announced United States Nuclear Tests, NVO-29 (Rev. 1), Department of Energy, Nevada Operations Office, January 1980.

claims.text: The force present: 'The Air Force arrayed 22 aircraft for the detonation', with WB-50 and U-2 weather aircraft, Navy P2Vs for surveillance and pod recovery and Marine helicopters, and nine Navy ships positioned to gather scientific data.

claims.source: DNA 6040F, Air Force aircraft participation in DOMINIC, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA136820/DTIC_ADA136820_djvu.txt
claims.text: KETTLE is a DOMINIC aircraft call sign, not a film. The aircraft participation table lists '3 / KC-135 / Kettle / Photographic aircraft' alongside Cognac, Kibosh, Cordova, Caboodle, Abusive, Lambkin, Baxter/Byron, Hewstone and White Spot. The strings 'RC-135' and 'Cobra' do not appear anywhere in the report.

claims.source: DNA 6040F, Operation DOMINIC I--1962, full-text search of the report, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA136820/DTIC_ADA136820_djvu.txt
claims.text: The report contains nothing of what is attached to this shot. It carries no reference to any unidentified object, unknown craft, anomalous observation, recovery or debris associated with the detonation; its only uses of 'unidentified' are an unidentified number of dosimetry analyses and one unidentified event in a fallout discussion. 'Gise' appears zero times in it, and so does Malmgren's name.

claims.text: DNA 6039F is not the FISHBOWL report. Its cover and Report Documentation Page both read 'OPERATION ARGUS 1958'. FISHBOWL appears instead in DNA 6040F's own keyword list.

desc: Bluegill Triple Prime was the fourth attempt to detonate the BLUEGILL device above Johnston Island, and the first that worked. Three earlier attempts failed: the 2 June 1962 launch was destroyed in flight after tracking was lost, BLUEGILL Prime burned on the pad, and BLUEGILL Double Prime failed on 15 October. The successful shot is recorded by the Defense Nuclear Agency at 25 October 1962, 2359 local, submegaton, tens of kilometres over Johnston Island, with 22 Air Force aircraft arrayed and nine Navy ships positioned to gather data. Four guests across four Michels lead maps attach a recovery story to it, and the record contradicts them in three places at once. The date is 25 October in the report's narrative and in its own Table 1, not 26 October, which is the GMT rendering of the same instant. DNA 6039F, cited for the shot in the candidates row, is Operation ARGUS 1958 and not the FISHBOWL report at all. And the report contains no unidentified object, no recovery, no debris, no RC-135 and no Cobra Ball: what it does carry is the call sign KETTLE, assigned to three KC-135 photographic aircraft, which is the documented origin of the Kettle film names the corpus uses. The node exists to hold the documented event so that the testimony has something dated to hang from.

timeline.label: Bluegill Triple Prime detonates over Johnston Island
timeline.text: The Defense Nuclear Agency's Operation DOMINIC I report records the shot at 25 October 1962, 2359 local, the fourth and first successful attempt to launch the BLUEGILL device on a Thor missile, submegaton, tens of kilometres over Johnston Island, with 22 Air Force aircraft arrayed and nine Navy ships positioned. The report carries no unidentified object, no recovery and no debris, and the photographic aircraft were three KC-135s under the call sign KETTLE.
